summary: PAPER-KALETHA-16 is a careful extraction of Kaletha's Rigid inner forms of real and p-adic groups: 157 items, 7 routes and 15 source issues. Its library items check out at the pins. Its handling of the author's errata is right, and E07 (the §3.4 H¹ = H¹_ab criterion fails for SL₂/R) re-derives independently. There are 13 findings: 1 high, 4 medium and 8 low. (1, high) Routes 3–4 put the rigid transfer factor (5.1), Proposition 5.6, (5.10), the adelic product and D34 into ET.0/ET.1, although they need D23, T44 and D31 from the route-7 Part II, whose first prerequisite is ET. That is a cycle, and the brief builds it in ('export ... to ET.1'). (2) HKW22 route 1 (HeckeStacksAndLocalShtukasKottwitzPartII, items 008–010) already plans rigid H¹, Corollaries 3.8/5.4, S_φ⁺ and the refined LLC, a second owner nobody reconciled. (3) Kottwitz's theorem [Kot86, Th. 1.2] has no item although Corollary 3.8, Lemma 4.9, §4.7, Corollary 5.4 and Lemma 5.7 use it; T44 drops Corollary 5.4's Z = 1 compatibility clause. (4) Degree-2 Tate–Nakayama and the vanishing of H² for anisotropic tori, which Theorem 4.8 and Corollary 3.7(1) rest on, have no item. (5) Real Harish-Chandra characters (P18) are routed to AF.1, which does not plan them; ET.1 says it constructs them. Low: (6) an unrecorded gap in the p-adic bijectivity proof of Corollary 3.8; (7) the review rewrote E04's printed field with the pre-publication display, which the published p. 586 has already corrected; (8) T54 states only one direction of Lemma 5.7; (9) P04's transgression belongs to Tau Ceti ProfiniteCohomology layer 5, not the proposed R02.2; (10) P02's degree-one Shapiro, colimit and corestriction are built at the pin; (11) Kot82 Cor. 2.2 and the Kottwitz sign e(G) have no items; (12) an unrecorded misprint in the proof of Theorem 3.1 (exponent (n_k/n_j)², wrong for F = R, harmless); (13) no sourceVersions field.

findings.where: PAPER-KALETHA-16 routes 3 and 4 (source → EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison:ET.0 / ET.1) against route 7 (part-ii EndoscopicTransferRigidInnerFormsPartII); items D33, T51, T52, D36, G05, G09 (route 4), D34 (route 3), P12 (planned ET.0)
findings.claim: The routing makes the parent roadmap depend on its own Part II, a cycle. Route 7 proposes EndoscopicTransferRigidInnerFormsPartII with EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison as its first prerequisite, and its items import ET.0/ET.1 (18 prerequisite edges into route 3, 3 into route 4). But routes 3 and 4 put into ET.0 and ET.1 items whose own prerequisites are Part II items. (i) Route 4 sends D33 (the rigid normalized absolute transfer factor (5.1)), T51 and T52 (Proposition 5.6), D36 ((5.10)), G05 and G09 to ET.1. D33 needs D23 (rigid stable-conjugacy invariant), T44 (the rigid pairing) and D31 (refined endoscopic data), all route 7. T52 needs T50 and D21, and G05 needs G04 and G02, all route 7. (ii) Conversely, route 7's R18 needs D36 and its G10 needs G09, both in ET.1, so ET.1 and the Part II each need the other. (iii) Route 3 sends D34 to ET.0 although D34 needs D23 (route 7). The planned item P12 (ordinary Tate–Nakayama at ET.0) lists R01 (the real Weil group, route 7) as a prerequisite. The route-7 brief builds the cycle in on purpose: it tells the Part II to 'export the rigid torus pairing to ET.1, which owns the actual transfer factor construction and global product' and to 'Export these to ET.1's unconditional adelic product'. A Part II must start where its parent stops (PROTOCOL §15). Otherwise ET.1's design would have to plan (5.1), Proposition 5.6, (5.10) and the §5.7 adelic product over objects that exist only in a roadmap built after it. The review accepted all seven routes without checking the direction of these edges.
findings.evidence: PROTOCOL §15: 'the additions form a roadmap that extends the existing one, titled "<existing roadmap>, Part II: <what it adds>", with the existing roadmap as its first prerequisite. It starts where the existing roadmap stops'. Route 4 reason: 'ET.1 already owns absolute normalizations, conventions, central extension transport and the global product formula. Add the rigid correction, its two convention signs, its relative-factor proof and the global rigid product/globalization adapters here'. Route 7 brief (PAPER-KALETHA-16.md): 'Build on Endoscopic transfer and unitary trace comparison ... as the first prerequisite. Import ET.1 transfer factors and their explicit conventions' and 'export the rigid torus pairing to ET.1, which owns the actual transfer factor construction and global product' and 'Export these to ET.1's unconditional adelic product and Arthur globalization theorem.' Prerequisite fields in PAPER-KALETHA-16.result.json: D33 [D23, T44, D31, D32]; T52 [D33, T50, D21]; G05 [G04, D33, G02]; D36 [D33, D32]; D34 [P12, P14, D23]; P12 [L26, L27, P07, R01, P06]; route-7 R18 [D36, R16, D30, P18]; route-7 G10 [G09, C01, G07]. findings.claim: Kottwitz's theorem [Kot86, Th. 1.2] has no item: the map H¹(F, G) → π₀(Z(Ĝ)^Γ)^D, bijective and a group isomorphism for p-adic F, functorial, and equal to Tate–Nakayama for tori. The paper uses it at five places. (a) The p-adic bijectivity in Corollary 3.8. (b) The proof of Lemma 4.9, which feeds Theorem 4.11 for every F, including F = R. (c) The group structure on H¹(u → W, Z → G) for p-adic F announced in §4.7 and its compatibility with Kottwitz's group structure. (d) The last sentence of Corollary 5.4: 'If Z = {1}, this pairing coincides with the one defined by Kottwitz in [Kot86]'. (e) The last step of Lemma 5.7. The introduction also claims the map 'is compatible with Kottwitz's map for any F and G'. The extraction lists Kot86 only as a prerequisite paper and in GAP04's deferred list ('Kneser, Kottwitz, Borovoi and Arthur inputs are cited suppliers' proofs'). No item states it, so no layer is asked to plan it. Two statements lose it as a result. T44 drops the Z = {1} compatibility clause of Corollary 5.4. T31 omits the p-adic group-structure statement of §4.7. The paper applies Th. 1.2 'If F is p-adic' in Corollary 3.8 but also in Lemmas 4.9 and 5.7, which serve F = R. So the item must say what is used over R: for example, that H¹(F, S) → H¹(F, G) and the abelianization factor through Borovoi's H¹_ab, which P13 plans at ET.0.

findings.where: PAPER-KALETHA-16 P12 (planned ET.0) and the prerequisites of T27 (Theorem 4.8), T12 (Corollary 3.7(1)) and T28 (§4.2); GAP04
findings.claim: Tate–Nakayama in degree 2 for tori has no item. This is the isomorphism Ĥ⁰(Γ_{E/F}, X_*(S)) = X_*(S)^Γ/N(X_*(S)) → H²(Γ_{E/F}, S(E)) given by cup product with the fundamental class. With it go two consequences: inflation H²(Γ_{E/F}, S(E)) → H²(Γ, S) is injective when E splits S, and H²(Γ, S) = 0 for an anisotropic torus S. The proof of Theorem 4.8, the main torus theorem, rests on it: its five-lemma needs the fourth vertical map to be injective, and the paper derives that from exactly these two facts. Corollary 3.7(1), which T12 records, rests on the vanishing of H² for anisotropic tori. The only Tate–Nakayama item, P12, states degree −1 → 1 only: '(X_*(S)_Gamma)_tors -> H1(F,S)'. None of T27, T12 or T28 lists an input for H². GAP04 mentions 'anisotropic H2 vanishing' only as deferred.
findings.evidence: Theorem 4.8 proof, printed p. 587: 'The right vertical map sends λ ∈ Y^Γ to λ ∪ c_k^{-1}; i.e., it is the composition of the negative of the Tate-Nakayama isomorphism Y^Γ/N_k(Y) → H²(Γ_{E_k/F}, S(E_k)) with the inclusion into H²(Γ, S).' and 'We also know that the fourth vertical map is injective, being given by a system of compositions ... → H²(Γ_{E_k/F}, S(E_k)) → H²(Γ, S), of which the first is bijective and the second injective.' Corollary 3.7 proof, p. 575: 'if S is an anisotropic torus, then H²(Γ, S) vanishes, so by (3.5) the map H¹(u → W, Z → S) → Hom(u, Z)^Γ is surjective'. Item P12 statement: 'For a local torus S split by finite Galois E/F, the fundamental class gives a natural isomorphism (X_*(S)_Gamma)_tors -> H1(F,S), and pairings for the two-term torus complexes ...'. Prerequisites: T27 [T20, T26, P12, T07]; T12 [P11, T10]; T28 [D13, D07, T12, P12, T12F]. The owners exist: tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ClassFieldTheory layer 0 plans 'the generic cup-product criterion of Tate's theorem ... and its Tate–Nakayama tensor-product generalization', layer 3 plans tateIso Ĥ^r(U/V, ℤ) ≃ Ĥ^{r+2}(U/V, A^V), and ET.0 plans 'local/global Tate–Nakayama pairings for tori'.
findings.fix: Extend P12, or add a planned item beside it, citing tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ClassFieldTheory#layer-0-audit-and-complete-the-cohomology-suppliers and #layer-3-tates-theorem-for-a-class-formation, and ET.0. It should say: for a torus S split by finite Galois E/F over a local field of characteristic 0, cup product with the fundamental class u_{E/F} gives Ĥ^i(Γ_{E/F}, X_*(S)) ≅ Ĥ^{i+2}(Γ_{E/F}, S(E)) for all i (in particular i = −1 and i = 0), compatibly with inflation and norms. findings.claim: P18 goes to the wrong owner. It is missing: Harish-Chandra distribution characters of admissible representations of real reductive groups, their conjugation invariance and their representation by a locally integrable function. Route 5 sends it to AF.1 on the grounds that AF.1 has an 'existing ... character foundation'. AF.1 plans (g,K)-modules, U(g) and infinitesimal characters, K-finiteness, Casselman–Wallach globalizations and relative Lie algebra cochains, and no distribution characters. findings.where: PAPER-KALETHA-16 sourceIssues (none at Corollary 3.8); items T14 and T13
findings.claim: The proof of Corollary 3.8 has a gap that no source issue records. For p-adic F and split G with Z = Z(G_der), the corollary asserts that H¹(u → W, Z → G) → H¹(Γ, Ḡ) is bijective. The printed proof shows that its kernel is trivial and that H¹(Γ, G) → H¹(Γ, G_ad) is injective. For a map of pointed sets that does not give injectivity. The paper's own Remark after Corollary 3.8 shows that non-neutral fibres of this map can be nontrivial over R. By twisting, the fibre through [z] is the kernel of the same map for the inner form G_z. By (3.6), and because ξ_* is injective for split Z (Proposition 3.2), that kernel is the image of H¹(Γ, Z) → H¹(Γ, G_z). The printed argument kills this image only for G_z = G, using a split maximal torus T of G (H¹(Γ, T) = 1), and G_z has none. The result is still true. Borovoi's H¹_ab depends only on the Γ-complex Z(G_sc) → Z(G), which is the same for all inner forms. So H¹(Γ, Z) → H¹_ab(G_z) is the same map as for G, which factors through H¹(Γ, T) = 0. For p-adic F, H¹(Γ, G_z) → H¹_ab(G_z) is injective by Kneser. So the image is trivial. Alternatively, count with Theorem 4.11, Proposition 5.3 and the remark after Corollary 5.4. Items T14/T14R copy the result without these inputs: T14's prerequisites are only T13 and P11.
findings.evidence: Corollary 3.8 proof, printed p. 576: 'the kernel of the first map in the corollary, which coincides with the kernel of the composition H¹(u → W, Z → G) → H¹(Γ, Ḡ) → H¹(Γ, G_ad), must be equal to the kernel of the map H¹(Γ, G) → H¹(Γ, G_ad). But this kernel is trivial. Indeed, it is enough to check that G_ad(F) → H¹(Γ, Z(G)) is surjective, but if T ⊂ G is a split maximal torus ... that suffices. If F is p-adic, then the map H¹(Γ, G) → H¹(Γ, G_ad) is actually a homomorphism of abelian groups [Kot86, Th. 1.2], and the triviality of its kernel implies its injectivity.' Remark, pp. 576–577: 'The following is a simple example that shows that some fibers of the first map in Corollary 3.8 can be nontrivial for F = R and G a split group ... The fiber of the surjection ... over the nontrivial element can be identified via twisting with the kernel of H¹(u → W, Z → G′) → H¹(Γ, G′_ad) ... The arguments of Corollary 3.8 show that this kernel is equal to the image of H¹(Γ, Z) → H¹(Γ, G′).' The same text is in arXiv v5. The author's errata §3 has no entry for Corollary 3.8 (its entries: Proposition 3.6, Section 4.4, Formula (4.8), Proof of Lemma 4.7, Corollary 5.4, Section 5.6). T14 prerequisites: [T13, P11].
findings.fix: Add a source issue: kind gap; locator Corollary 3.8, proof of the p-adic bijectivity, printed p. 576; affects the proof; known new; searched: the author's errata §3 and arXiv v5. Printed: the two quoted sentences. Correction: for each inner twist G_z, the image of H¹(Γ, Z) in H¹(Γ, G_z) is trivial. It lies in the kernel of H¹(Γ, G_z) → H¹_ab(Γ, G_z) = H¹(Γ, Z(G_sc) → Z(G)), a map independent of z that factors through H¹(Γ, T) = 1 for a split maximal torus T of G, and that kernel is trivial for p-adic F by Kneser. So every fibre is a singleton. Add P11 (Kneser), P13 (H¹_ab) and the Kottwitz item of finding 3 to T14's prerequisites.

findings.claim: T54 states only one direction of Lemma 5.7, which is an 'exactly' statement. The lemma says the characters of π₀(Z(\hat{\bar G})⁺) that annihilate the kernel of (5.12) are precisely those that correspond to K-groups of rigid inner twists for which φ is relevant. T54 says only that a character trivial on the kernel 'corresponds under T44 to a relevant K-group'. It omits the converse, that the character of a relevant K-group kills the kernel. That converse is the 'part of our claim' §5.5 opens with. The proof of Proposition 5.9 needs both directions: it concludes that the image of (5.15) 'coincides with the group of characters ... that are trivial on the kernel of (5.12)' and compares cardinalities. R15 and R16 depend on T54.
findings.evidence: Lemma 5.7, printed p. 611: 'The characters of π₀(Z(\hat{\bar G})⁺) that annihilate the kernel of (5.12) are precisely those that correspond to K-groups of rigid inner twists of G for which ϕ is relevant.' §5.5 opening, p. 610: 'part of our claim is the following: If a tempered Langlands parameter ϕ is relevant for an inner form G′ of G that is part of a rigid inner twist (G′, ψ, z), then the character of π₀(Z(\hat{\bar G})⁺) that corresponds to the class of z must annihilate the kernel of the map (5.12)'. Proposition 5.9 proof, p. 621: 'By Lemma 5.7 this image coincides with the group of characters of π₀(Z(\hat{\bar G})⁺) that are trivial on the kernel of (5.12), and this shows that the cardinalities of the images of (5.12) and (5.15) coincide.' T54 statement: 'A character of pi0 Z(Gbar_hat)^+ trivial on the kernel of its map to pi0 S_phi^+ corresponds under T44 to a relevant K-group for phi; over R this is a K-group condition ...'.
findings.fix: Restate T54 as an equivalence. For a tempered φ and a K-group of rigid inner twists realized by Z (a class in H¹_ab(u → W, Z → G), identified by T44 with a character of π₀(Z(\hat{\bar G})⁺)), φ is relevant for some inner form in that K-group if and only if the character is trivial on ker(π₀(Z(\hat{\bar G})⁺) → π₀(S_φ⁺)). Every character trivial on that kernel comes from a K-group.

findings.claim: The proof of Theorem 3.1 contains a misprint that no source issue records. For the H² step of the vanishing of H¹(Γ, u), it says p restricted to the diagonal μ_{n_k} ⊂ R_k 'is the (n_k/n_j)²-power map'. By (3.2), p sends a constant map x to x^{[E_k:E_j]·n_k/n_j}. The printed exponent is right only under the choice n_k = [E_k:F], which the proof makes for non-archimedean F and in the H² paragraph only. For F = R, E_k = C for k ≥ 1, so [E_k:E_j] = 1 and the map is the n_k/n_j-power. That map does not kill μ_{n_j}, so the stated reason fails. The conclusion survives. H²(Γ_R, μ_n) = μ_n^Γ/N(μ_n) is {±1} for even n and 0 for odd n. The map sends −1 to (−1)^{n_k/n_j} = 1, because n_j | n_k/n_j and n_j = j! is even. So nothing is affected.
findings.evidence: Theorem 3.1 proof, printed p. 572: 'For the case of H²(Γ, μ_{n_k}), we note that the restriction of the map p to the diagonally embedded copy of μ_{n_k} into R_k is the (n_k/n_j)²-power map. We then choose k so that n_k/n_j is a multiple of n_j.' Earlier, p. 571: 'If F is nonarchimedean, we can clarify the situation by setting n_k = [E_k : F].' (3.2), p. 570: '(pf)(a) = ∏_{b ∈ Γ_{K/F}, b ↦ a} f(b)^{m/n}', which for f ≡ x has [K:E] factors. Theorem 5.2 proof, p. 595: 'We set E_k = C for all k, n_k = k!'. arXiv v5 has the same sentence. The errata §3 has no entry for Theorem 3.1.
findings.fix: Add a source issue: kind misprint; locator Theorem 3.1, proof, H² step, printed p. 572; affects nothing; known new. Correction: 'the [E_k:E_j]·(n_k/n_j)-power map, which equals the (n_k/n_j)²-power map when n_k = [E_k:F]; for F = R it is the (n_k/n_j)-power map, which is zero on H²(Γ, μ_{n_k}) since that group is killed by 2 and n_k/n_j is even'. T02's proof steps should use the corrected exponent.
